WITH s2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM trips WHERE fish_date_season = 2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 213 AND 244
)
SELECT
  cls,
  (fish_date_doy / 10)::int * 10 AS bucket,
  SUM(yt) AS yt_sum,
  SUM(anglers) AS anglers_sum,
  COUNT(*) AS n_trips,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::float / NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0), 3) AS ypa
FROM s2
WHERE cls IN ('three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5')
GROUP BY cls, bucket
ORDER BY bucket, cls;

SELECT boat, cls,
  SUM(yt) AS yt_sum, SUM(anglers) AS anglers_sum, COUNT(*) AS n,
  ROUND(SUM(yt)::float / NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0),3) AS ypa
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 213 AND 244
  AND boat IN ('Ranger 85','Sea Adventure 80','Cortez','New Lo-An')
  AND cls IN ('overnight','day_1_5')
GROUP BY boat, cls
ORDER BY boat, cls;

# dope_solo notes — living doc. Read top section first (current plan), history below.

## CURRENT PLAN — as of Season 2, day 244 planning turn (21:00)
Status: **$100/$2000 left, 8/10 PTO, season score 0.0958, rank 23/34.** Cumulative
score still 0 (S1-S2 are practice). Confirmed via journal d213-d243: nightly-self
correctly stayed in observation-only mode every single night — $100 is below the
$150 THREE_QUARTER floor, let alone $400 overnight / $550 day_1_5. **Nothing is
bookable for the rest of S2 (d244-335) at any signal strength.** Do not spend more
tool-budget re-verifying this each planning turn — it's arithmetic, not a judgment
call, until budget changes (it won't; season ends d335). Only value left this
season: watch data build for the S3 plan.

## THIS TURN'S FINDING: day_1_5 became the dominant class doy210-244, on LARGE
## samples — and it beat every individual "watchlist boat," which reframes the
## boat-picking theory from last turn.
Pulled S2 class-pooled ypa by 10-day bucket, doy210-244 (n = trip count, not angler count):

| bucket | day_1_5 ypa | overnight ypa | three_quarter ypa |
|---|---|---|---|
| doy210-219 | 1.181 (n=3, small) | 0.067 (n=1) | 0.064 (n=10) |
| doy220-229 | 0.342 (n=31) | 0.022 (n=31) | 0.061 (n=68) |
| doy230-239 | 0.379 (n=48) | 0.006 (n=25) | 0.026 (n=42) |
| doy240-244(partial) | 0.176 (n=43) | 0.028 (n=44) | 0.05 (n=42) |

Two things this changes from the d213 note:
1. **Overnight's doy190-213 breakout (0.318 ypa) did NOT continue** — it fully
   collapsed by doy220 (0.022, 0.006, 0.028) while **day_1_5 took over and sustained
   0.34-0.38 ypa across 79 combined trips (doy220-239)** — a big, high-confidence,
   fleet-wide number, not a single-boat fluke. So the S2 pattern is: ONI crosses
   ~-0.5 around doy190 → overnight spikes briefly (doy190-213) → day_1_5 takes over
   and sustains for a full month+ (doy210-240+). Overnight is the *early* tell, not
   the payoff; day_1_5 is where the real edge accumulates.
2. **Boat-specific watchlist underperformed the class-pooled number this window** —
   checked Ranger 85 (day_1_5 ypa 0.128, n=5), New Lo-An (0.10, n=8), Cortez (0.025,
   n=2), Sea Adventure 80 (0.385, n=2, too small to trust) against doy220-239's day_1_5411
   overrode class-wide 0.34-0.38. Every named boat except the tiny-sample Sea
   Adventure 80 trip did *worse* than just betting the class. **Lesson: the S1→S2
   "hot boat" watchlist was likely overfit to small samples (n=2-9) from a single
   prior window.** For S3, weight the CLASS-POOLED trailing ypa (8-14 trip, fleet-wide)
   above individual boat picks unless a specific boat's own trailing sample is also
   large (n>8) and clearly beats the class pool — don't chase a boat off 2-3 trips.
3. ONI: -0.5 (doy191) → -0.34 (doy221) — still warming, but decelerating vs the
   April-August pace (-1.57→-0.5 over doy9-191). Consistent with "ONI crossing
   ~-0.5/-0.6 is the trigger point" theory from last turn; nothing here breaks it,
   ONI is now solidly past that threshold and multi-day classes are working.

## REVISED SEASON 3 PLAN (supersedes d213 version)
1. **Track ONI from day 1.** Treat ONI crossing roughly -0.6 to -0.5 as the trigger
   to start watching OVERNIGHT class-pooled ypa closely (it's the early tell), and
   expect DAY_1_5 to take over ~2-4 weeks after overnight spikes, then sustain at
   high ypa (0.3-0.4+ fleet-wide) for a month or more. Don't wait for calendar
   doy240 — in S2 this whole cycle ran doy190-240, ~50-60 days earlier than S1's
   equivalent (doy240-335) window.
2. **Cap spring/summer THREE_QUARTER probing spend hard: ~$300-450 (2-3 trips
   max)**, only on boats with an 8+ trip trailing pooled ypa >0.25-0.3. S2 spent
   $1650 on 12 3Q/overnight probes for a 0.0958 season score — that overspend is
   the single reason the doy190-240 day_1_5 breakout (worth multiples of the whole
   season, at 0.34-0.38 ypa on 79 trips) was completely unreachable by the time it
   hit ($100 left by d181).
3. **Reserve $1600+ and 6+ PTO specifically for the OVERNIGHT→DAY_1_5 cycle.**
   Budget for roughly 2-3 real DAY_1_5 shots at $550 each (~$1100-1650) plus a
   couple of $400 overnight probes to catch the early tell. This is a bigger reserve
   than the d213 note's $1400 — day_1_5 is confirmed the highest-value class two
   seasons running (S1 doy300-335: 1.875 ypa; S2 doy210-240: 0.34-0.38 ypa on
   n=79) and it's expensive, so don't let it get bid down to "whatever's left."
4. **PTO timing matters as much as budget**: PTO must commit 14 days ahead. If ONI
   crosses the ~-0.5/-0.6 trigger around doy150-190 like it did in S2, start
   pre-committing PTO for weekday day_1_5/overnight dates in that window *before*
   confirmation shows up in the counts, or the 14-day lag will lock out the early
   part of the breakout the same way the budget lock did in S2. Don't wait for a
   boat-level trigger to commit PTO — commit on the ONI/overnight early-tell signal.
5. **Trust class-pooled trailing ypa over boat picks** unless a boat's own trailing
   n>8 and clearly beats the pool (see finding #2 above) — the S1/S2 "boat
   watchlist" (Ranger 85, Sea Adventure 80, New Lo-An, Cortez) was built on small
   samples and did not hold up against the class-wide number in this window. Still
   worth checking per-boat before booking (in case one boat really is running hot),
   but don't pre-commit to a boat list — evaluate live each time.
6. **3Q is not where the fall/mid-season edge lives**, confirmed a third time now
   (S1 doy240-300, S2 doy182-213, S2 doy210-244 all show 3Q flat 0.03-0.12 while
   overnight/day_1_5 break out). Stop treating 3Q as the default cheap probe once
   ONI warms past ~-0.6; shift the early probing budget toward a couple of cheap
   overnight trips instead — they're the leading indicator for day_1_5, not just an
   alternative to it.
7. HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: confirmed dead all year, two seasons running, every
   window checked. Never book. Fully settled, no need to re-verify.

## Next planning turn checks
1. If this is the S2 season-end turn: lock in the S3 numeric plan above ($300-450
   spring 3Q cap, $1600+ reserve for overnight→day_1_5 cycle, PTO pre-commit on
   ONI trigger not boat confirmation).
2. Pull S2 doy244-335 as it becomes available (even though unactionable this
   season) — does day_1_5 ypa keep decaying (0.379→0.176 already looks like it's
   rolling over) or does it re-spike for a second peak like S1's doy300-335? This
   tells us whether S2's cycle is one broad hump (doy190-240) already past peak, or
   whether a second wave is still coming — matters for how early/late to pre-commit
   S3 PTO.
3. Check S1's ONI trajectory at the doy150-200 equivalent point (still open from
   d213 note, never actually pulled) — confirms or kills the "ONI ~-0.5/-0.6 is the
   real clock, not day-of-year" theory with a second season of ONI data.
4. Re-run the boat-level day_1_5/overnight check for doy244+ once posted — does any
   boat actually separate from the class pool with a larger sample (n>8), or does
   finding #2 (class beats boats) hold up further?

---

## Season-1 baseline reference (by class, doy bucket, ypa) — kept for comparison.
- HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: dead all year, both seasons (~0.00-0.01). Never book.
- doy80-100: pooled 0.833 (spring spike).
- doy120-180: three_quarter 0.467, overnight 0.5, day_1_5 0.239 (S1 only).
- doy180-240: weak across the board in S1 (3Q 0.049, overnight 0.144, day_1_5
  0.02) — S2's doy182-213 broke this pattern (overnight 0.318, day_1_5 0.328), and
  doy210-240 (this turn's pull) shows day_1_5 sustaining 0.34-0.38 while overnight
  faded. S1 and S2 do NOT share this window's shape — treat every season's
  doy180-240 as unknown until the live data says otherwise.
- doy240-300 (S1): day_1_5 0.8, overnight 0.272, 3Q 0.122 (fall ramp-up).
- doy300-335 (S1): **day_1_5 1.875 (best of anywhere)**, overnight 0.184, 3Q 0.055.
- doy335+: dead (season ending).

## Season 2 timeline log (condensed)
- Doy1-91: cold La Niña start (ONI ~-1.6 to -1.3), trips table flat 0.000 through
  doy91 despite S1's spring spike there.
- Doy91-182: 12 cheap 3Q/overnight probes total, following trailing-ypa discipline.
  Only 2 non-zero results (d100 share 0.024, d181 share 0.071) out of 12. Budget
  went from $2000 to $100. doy152-182 confirmed a genuine 3Q/overnight/day_1_5
  trough.
- Doy182-213: stayed home (budget-locked) — exactly when overnight (0.318) and
  day_1_5 (0.328) broke out. Missed entirely due to budget spent earlier, not bad
  judgment in the moment.
- Doy210-244: day_1_5 took over from overnight and sustained 0.34-0.38 ypa on 79
  pooled trips (doy220-239), rolling over some by doy240-244 (0.176). Also missed
  entirely — still budget-locked at $100.
- ONI trend S2: -1.57 (doy9) → -1.29 (doy71) → -1.06 (doy99) → -0.85 (doy130) →
  -0.68 (doy160) → -0.50 (doy191) → -0.34 (doy221). Steady warming all season,
  decelerating slightly by doy220.
- Doy244-335: not yet pulled (future turns / next season's history).

## Open items
- No forum/submit_strategy tool available to this agent (solo variant) — decisions
  are notes.md + nightly briefing judgment only.
- Leaderboard (as of d244): skeptic_solo 0.83, persist_solo 0.72, calendarist 0.70
  lead; dope_solo 0.0958, rank 23/34. Top public strategy strings are all "books
  nothing" (solo variant quirk — real bookings are nightly judgment, strategy.py
  unused) so no way to read their approach from strategy text; their edge is
  presumably better budget pacing into the high-ypa windows, which is exactly
  what the S3 plan above is trying to fix.
- S1 doy150-200 ONI trajectory: still not pulled — do this next turn (item #3
  above), it's the key second-season test of the ONI-as-clock theory.
